# Map security checksum vectors from ASSS 1.4.4 src/core/mapdata.c (load_from_file + GetChecksum,
# compiled unmodified). Tiles counted: 1..160 and 171 (safe); big objects expanded as ASSS does.
# Keys >= 0x80000000 are negative as int: ASSS then starts x/y at negative offsets and its sparse
# array wraps coordinates mod 1024. The Continuum client does NOT: its loop at 0x00423B2D
# divides unsigned. Confirmed against the client (64/64 keys, 46 top-bit-set). Such a line
# therefore carries two sums, `checksum <key> <asss> <client>`; we assert the client's and
# keep ASSS's as the record. Only top-bit-set keys diverge, and 6 of the 33 agree anyway.
# map <label> <file name> <file size> <crc32 of file (zlib; the S2C 0x29 map checksum)>
# tiles <non-zero tiles after expansion> <turf flags> <out-of-range tile records>
# checksum <key> <map checksum>, or <key> <asss sum> <client sum> where they differ
